- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (≥0.67) — apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates the drop — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model fails to capture immediate mean reversion — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for the next 7–10 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often lags — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast for the next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–15% if sentiment is volatile or event-driven.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model over-optimistic — reduce forecast by 3–5% for the next 7–10 days.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal after a spike, model fails to adjust — apply “reversal buffer” rule: if forecast > true outcome by >10%, reduce by 15–20% for next 5 days.
